pk.context: 500 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Oral bioavailability is 95%, and more than 99% of the drug is bound to albumin. About 95% of a dose is excreted in urine, mostly as conjugates.
clues.substance: An odorless crystalline substance with a molecular weight of 230.26.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in 250 mg, 375 mg and 500 mg strengths, usually given twice daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning on serious cardiovascular thrombotic events. Contraindicated around bypass graft surgery and after asthma or urticaria from aspirin; gastrointestinal complaints are most frequent.
clues.indication: Relief of the signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and juvenile arthritis.
clues.mechanism: It belongs to the NSAID group, but this label describes no specific enzyme or receptor target.

tell: Its 12-to-17-hour half-life stays the same across formulations, which sets this NSAID apart.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The plasma half-life of the naproxen anion in humans ranges from 12 to 17 hours
